scenarios.title: Repair offline filesystem accounting without losing files
scenarios.summary: Investigate named files, allocation records and offline repair while protecting another volume.
scenarios.objective: Repair all supported consistency findings on /dev/vdb1 without changing report.txt or its original data blocks. Restore /dev/vdb1 mounted at /mnt/data. Leave /dev/vdc1 and its mount at /mnt/notes exactly unchanged.
steps: Investigate the supplied virtual volume, repair only supported findings, verify retained contents and restore access.
scenarios.explanation: The stored allocation maps and link counts must agree with actual file references. Unmounting alone changes no accounting. Offline preen corrects supported link, bitmap and summary disagreements while retaining the report and its blocks. A fresh read-only check reports no remaining findings; remounting restores access without touching the separate notes volume.
hints: Inspect findmnt first: a mountpoint is where files are accessed; the device is what the checker examines.
A read-only check diagnoses; it does not repair. Unmount only the target and read the reported remaining finding.
Preen handles supported accounting errors. After repair, recheck offline and restore the mount. The protected notes volume must remain exactly unchanged.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded original ext-family graph: fixed root/lost+found, retained file bytes and block ownership, names, link counts, allocation maps and free totals. No raw ext4/journal parser, disk I/O, missing-byte reconstruction, shared-block repair, arbitrary directories, kernel, real commands or mount effects. Mounted-check refusal is a stricter exercise policy. ls owner/mode/time are fixed modeled metadata. See FS_INTEGRITY_SUBSET.md.

scenarios.title: Recover retained unnamed data and restore access
scenarios.summary: Distinguish automatic correction from explicit recovery, inspect lost+found and preserve retained bytes.
scenarios.objective: Repair all supported consistency findings on /dev/vdb1 without changing report.txt or its original data blocks. Reconnect each supplied nonempty unnamed file in lost+found, preserving its original bytes and data blocks. A read-only check or automatic repair alone is insufficient. Restore /dev/vdb1 mounted at /mnt/data. Leave /dev/vdc1 and its mount at /mnt/notes exactly unchanged.
steps: Investigate the supplied virtual volume, repair only supported findings, verify retained contents and restore access.
scenarios.explanation: The directory name, file inode and its retained data are different facts. Preen refuses the nonempty unnamed inode because reconnecting it needs an explicit decision. In this supplied exercise, explicit recovery attaches retained bytes under lost+found, choosing a different name if needed; it does not reconstruct overwritten data. Recheck, remount and read the recovered content. The separate notes volume remains unchanged.
hints: Inspect findmnt first: a mountpoint is where files are accessed; the device is what the checker examines.
A read-only check diagnoses; it does not repair. Unmount only the target and read the reported remaining finding.
Preen handles supported accounting errors. A nonempty unnamed inode needs an explicit recovery decision in this exercise; inspect the name actually chosen under lost+found.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded original ext-family graph: fixed root/lost+found, retained file bytes and block ownership, names, link counts, allocation maps and free totals. No raw ext4/journal parser, disk I/O, missing-byte reconstruction, shared-block repair, arbitrary directories, kernel, real commands or mount effects. Mounted-check refusal is a stricter exercise policy. ls owner/mode/time are fixed modeled metadata. See FS_INTEGRITY_SUBSET.md.
